neighbours.label: Function words inside a well-known text being recited verbatim (proverbs, scripture, famous quotations, textbook theorems): the square |of| the hypotenuse, everything looks |like| a nail, |may| the Lord …; not the same sentence shapes with made-up content
fire: As the old proverb says, a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
The preacher began: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures.
Everyone knows the line: ask not what your country can do for you, ask what you can do for your country.
Remember the rule from school: for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.
As the saying has it, the early bird catches the worm, and a stitch in time saves nine.
She quoted Dickens: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.
He recited: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name; thy kingdom come, thy will be done.
The teacher wrote on the board: the area of a circle is equal to pi times the square of the radius.
quiet: As the old gardener says, a rake in the shed is worth less than a bucket by the door.
The preacher began: The mayor is my neighbour; I shall not complain. He allows me to park beside his fence.
Everyone knows the notice: bring only what your office can spare for us, bring it before Friday.
Remember the note from school: for every trip there is a short and boring form.
As the memo has it, the late bus reaches the depot, and a call at noon saves time.
She quoted her aunt: It was the dullest of picnics, it was the wettest of weekends.
He recited: Our landlord, who lives in Leeds, wants the rent on Monday; the plumber may come, the roof will be fixed.
The teacher wrote on the board: the price of a ticket is equal to four times the cost of the lunch.

notes: Probes: hammer/nail proverb 0.90, Pythagoras 0.63, priestly blessing 0.48, 'To be, or not to be' 0.37, 'journey of a thousand miles' 0.35; invented sentences with the same shapes 0.02-0.04.
